finalText:
The new **Settings** canvas is at `ui/Settings.tsx`. It has four desktop artboards (1440 × 1024) in the maude design system, side by side. Strict checks pass with no errors, and I looked at a screenshot of each artboard; all four render styled and nothing runs off the bottom edge.

All four pages share one layout. Across the top is the Maude menubar, showing "Settings / *page*" and "Changes save as you go". On the left is a settings menu with search, where the current page is the only accent colour. The right side holds grouped panels, each row a label, a one-line description and a control. All the controls are the design system's own (switches, segmented controls, selects, inputs, checkboxes, buttons).

- **General:** theme, interface density and language; canvas options (dot grid, snapping, nudge distance in px, design system for new canvases); start-up behaviour.
- **Account:** a sample profile (Mira Novak) with name and role fields; signed-in services (Claude, GitHub connected; Figma not connected); the Maude Cloud team plan with 5 of 8 seats used; a "Leave" group with Sign out and Delete account….
- **Notifications:** a table of six events (mentions, replies, AI run finished, teammate publishes, access requests, export ready) against In app / Desktop / Email checkboxes; an email digest; quiet hours.
- **Privacy:** an info note that canvases stay on disk; presence settings; AI settings (Search in pictures is off; keep or clear chat history); crash reports, usage statistics and "Download my data".

Two places where I didn't follow the design-system check's hints, because following them broke the canvas:
- **CSS imports kept.** The check says the studio supplies the maude styles itself, but without the two imports the screenshot came out completely unstyled. I put them back, as `GitPanel.tsx` does. The check still flags this as a warning.
- **Local icons.** The design system's `<Icon>` draws an empty box, because maude names its icons but ships no artwork for them. I drew small line icons in the canvas instead. The check warns about inline SVG for these; that's expected.

I didn't run the optional design critic. I tried to save a note about these two issues to memory for future sessions, but writing to the memory folder was blocked, so it isn't saved.
